feature: A smooth slide into Edit mode
summary: Pressing Cmd-2 on a recording in View now slides the panel, tool bar and tracks in as smoothly as Cmd-1 slides them out. The panel's sections, the tool bar and the track rows now fill in right after the slide lands instead of during it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a long recording with captions (five minutes is where it showed), so it opens in View.

try.do: Press Cmd-2 and watch the panel slide in from the right.
Watch the moment the slide stops: the panel and tracks are still empty.
Watch the tool bar, the track rows and the panel's sections fill in.
Press Cmd-1, then Cmd-2 again, and compare the two slides.
Press Cmd-2 then Cmd-1 quickly, inside a quarter second, and check the window lands in View cleanly.

evaluate: Does the slide into Edit now feel as smooth as the slide back to View?
Does the panel and tracks filling in just after the slide read as intended, or as the app catching up?
Is the fill-in quick enough that you never try to click something that is not there yet?
On a short recording with no captions, does anything about the switch feel different from before?
rough: The editor's contents land about 0.3 to 0.7s after the key on a five minute captioned recording, visibly after the slide. The pieces cost the same to build as before, they just no longer land while things move. Filed as a follow-up: make them cheap enough to come with the slide.
The main thread is still busy about 630 to 680ms of the 0.8s after Cmd-2, so this task's second check (well under half) is not met. The time is the same; it no longer lands in the slide.
Pictures are from a walk's film of the window below the title bar, at half size.
